bindings.domain: Distinct source copy construction: explicit fallible copy-constructor policy or explicit T:Copy trivial policy. Failed callback Err retains completed and incomplete values until Rust recovery.
Distinct source copy operator=: explicit constructor; assign_trivial(source,false) selects source allocator for trivial copying.

Distinct source Assign: own_allocator true/false; explicit constructor or T:Copy trivial policy, plus refreshed existing Clone convenience delegation. Native self-assignment continues to use existing assign_self adapter.

behavior: Public from_copied_with supports explicit fallible copy construction without Clone, Default or copy-assignment bounds. Each native block allocation precedes element construction; only completely copied blocks become published. Retained empty blocks are copied too.

Public assign_with_constructor first clears old elements and blocks, copies source stride, and optionally adopts source allocator; copy operator adapter selects adoption. Existing Clone assignment delegates this same policy engine without changing its panic convenience behavior.

Native throwing copy construction leaks completed payload blocks and the incomplete payload block, although its pointer-table member unwinds. DynamicArrayCopyConstructionFailure keeps both groups alive for pre-recovery observation. published_array/copy_failure inspect them; into_parts moves ownership without cleaning up first. Drop is explicitly Rust recovery.

The native nonassignable/nondefault Item throws on each of three constructor attempts. Sixteen rows compare events with allocation counts inside constructor/destructor callbacks, complete-prefix metadata, partial values, allocator identity, and total live items. Failed constructor rows inspect known live leaked slots and derived publication, never access an unconstructed owner.

Nine trivial rows cover empty unallocated source, empty retained three-block source, and partially filled last block with retained third block, in construction and both Assign allocator policies. Rust T:Copy policy bypasses an observable Clone implementation.

Direct owner Drop/into_parts recover all values, and callback panic uses ordinary Rust RAII. Empty unsigned-overflow source copies preserve wrapped zero stride. Element allocation guards are reused from the integrated overflow work.

All52 original legacy names join both normal and strict Miri logs. Five new policy methods have unique reachable body-bearing compiler declarations: three have unbounded T and two require only T:Copy. Existing Assign body capture is refreshed after shared-engine delegation.
limitations: Explicit selection of constructor and trivial-copy policies replaces C++ trait inference; automatic trait dispatch is not implemented. Rust T:Copy is an intentionally narrower representable domain than all C++ is_trivially_copyable types.

Failure ownership preserves payload lifetimes before recovery, but keeps Rust descriptor storage and allocator ownership alive. Native pointer-table destructor timing, released allocator handles, and permanent payload leaks are not replicated. Those resource-lifetime domains remain actionable gaps.

Native constructor throws must be returned as Err. Rust callback panic performs RAII cleanup and differs from native constructor leak behavior; panic recovery is tested as a Rust extension. Allocation failure, descriptor allocation/growth failure, and throwing destructors are outside this recoverable error domain.

Native distinct-object assignment is covered here. Safe Rust does not permit simultaneous mutable receiver and shared donor aliases; existing assign_self handles self-assignment and this batch does not add another alias.

Layout-changing retained strides, zero-stride retained-block mutations, C++ padding-byte identity, zero-sized Rust payloads, ABI and cross-platform widths remain outside these probes. Checked source/storage rejection is a Rust extension, not general native undefined-behavior classification.
validation_scope: Final source passes20 DynamicArray integration targets (281 tests),21 units, strict Clippy/fmt and89 strict Miri tests. Both native probes compile with UBSan; linked TKernel remains prebuilt. Three exact native declarations bind five new callable policies plus the refreshed existing Assign body. No shared ledger or raw lifetime helper edits.
